entry.content:
This guide will walk you through the process of installing RStudio on Vanilla OS 22.10 Kinetic using an apt (Ubuntu) container.

Initial Setup

First, we need to prepare the apt container and install the necessary prerequisites. Open your terminal and run the following commands:

Enter the apt container:

apx enter apt

Install common software properties:

sudo apt install --no-install-recommends software-properties-common dirmngr

Install required libraries:

sudo apt install libasound2
sudo apt install libnss3

Update and upgrade your system:

sudo apt update
sudo apt upgrade

Downloading and Installing RStudio

Next, download the RStudio Desktop .deb file from the official source: RStudio Desktop 2023.06.2-561

Once the download is complete, install it by running:

cd Downloads
ls
sudo dpkg -i rstudio-2023.06.2-561-amd64.deb

Note: If you encounter any dependency errors during installation, run sudo apt --fix-broken install and then repeat the dpkg command.

Installing R

To run RStudio, you also need to install R. Add the official R repository and install the base package:

Add the R repository:

sudo add-apt-repository "deb https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu $(lsb_release -cs)-cran40/"

Add the public key:

wget -qO- https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu/marutter_pubkey.asc | sudo tee -a /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/cran_ubuntu_key.asc

Install R Base:

sudo apt install r-base

Utilizing RStudio

With everything installed, you can now launch RStudio directly from your terminal by typing:

rstudio

Useful Commands

Command Function
apx enter apt Enters the apt (Ubuntu) container
rstudio Launches the RStudio application
R --version Displays the installed R version
exit Exits the current directory or container
sudo apt update Fetches available updates
sudo apt upgrade Installs available updates

entry.content:
Students have long faced difficulties with McGraw-Hill’s online accounting textbooks due to strict copy prevention measures. This restriction not only prevents offline reading but also hampers studying and taking digital notes on practice problems. While some have attempted to bypass this by changing browser settings, McGraw-Hill uses JavaScript to enforce their copy protection. Fortunately, there is a solution that does not require circumventing their systems: NormCap.

NormCap is an open-source, OCR-powered screenshot tool that allows users to extract text from almost anything on their screen, including images, videos, and protected websites like McGraw-Hill Connect. Instead of capturing a traditional image, NormCap detects and extracts the text directly to your clipboard.

To get started, simply download and install NormCap from their official website. Once running, select the region of text you wish to copy, and it will automatically be added to your clipboard for easy pasting. It is a completely free tool without ads, designed to help students easily capture notes and focus on their coursework.

Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Download and Install Download the application from the official NormCap website.

  2. Launch the Application Start NormCap. A pink border will appear once the necessary permissions are granted.

  3. Select Text Highlight the region of text you wish to copy. The text is now automatically copied to your clipboard.

  4. Paste Your Text Press Ctrl+V (or your system’s paste shortcut) to paste the text anywhere.

Note: Settings can be accessed by starting NormCap or pressing “Capture” in the tray icon while the app is running. As of version 0.4.1, settings are located in the top right corner of the screen.

entry.title: How to Convert PDFs to Images with GIMP

entry.content:
Introduction

Sometimes you may need to convert a PDF to an image PDF, which is a PDF file that contains images instead of text displayed over images. This can be useful for a variety of reasons, such as when you want to preserve the formatting of the original PDF or when you want to share the PDF with others who may not have the same fonts installed on their computer. This can also be used to prevent getting falsely accused of plagiarizing with AI software.

Fortunately, GIMP, the popular open-source image editing software, can be used to easily convert a PDF to an image PDF. Here’s how to do it:

Instructions

  1. Install GIMP First, you need to have GIMP installed on your computer. If you don’t have it already, you can download it for free from the official GIMP website.

  2. Open the PDF File in GIMP Once you have GIMP installed, open it and go to File > Open to open the PDF file you want to convert to an image PDF.

  3. Import Pages as Layers GIMP will show a dialog box asking you how you want to import the PDF file. Choose the Open pages as Layers option, and click Import. GIMP will then import each page of the PDF as a separate image. You can view these images by clicking on the Layers tab on the right-hand side of the screen.

  4. Export as PDF To export the images to an image PDF, go to File > Export As. In the Export Image dialog box, choose a location to save the image PDF file, and give it a name. Under Select File Type, choose PDF from the drop-down menu. Click on the Export button to convert the images to a PDF.

  5. Choose PDF Export Options In the Export Images as PDF dialog box, make sure the Layers as pages (bottom layers first) option is selected, and click Export.

  6. Save the Image PDF File GIMP will then save the image PDF file to the location you specified. You can now view and use the image PDF file just like any other PDF file.

That’s it! With these steps, you can easily convert a PDF to an image PDF using GIMP. Converting a PDF to an image PDF can be a useful skill to have, especially if you work with PDF files frequently. Give it a try and see how it can benefit you!

entry.content:
Overview

When your Lenovo IdeaPad 5 (14ITL05) loses internet access—shown by the globe icon—you can fix the Wi-Fi driver using another computer.

Steps

  1. Prepare another device Use a separate laptop with internet to open Lenovo’s site. Search “Lenovo IdeaPad 5 (14ITL05) drivers” and download the newest Windows 11 Wi-Fi driver, or use the direct link.

  2. Transfer the driver Insert a USB drive into the working laptop and copy the downloaded file.

  3. Install on the IdeaPad Plug the USB into your Lenovo IdeaPad 5 (14ITL05), open the drive, and double-click 37sw0a0f43gwseb0.exe. Confirm administrator permission if prompted, then complete the installation.

  4. Restart Reboot the laptop so changes take effect.

Notes

  • Check Lenovo’s support site for the latest driver and other updates.
  • Back up essential files before updating.
